sentences.text: Det var koldt, og sneen faldt over byen.
sentences.translation: It was cold, and the snow fell over the town.

words.grammar: en sne · sneen (the snow) · uncountable
falde (to fall) · faldt (past) · er faldet (perfect) · strong verb

sentences.text: En lille pige gik alene på gaden.
sentences.translation: A little girl walked alone on the street.

words.grammar: alene = alone · manner adverb, modifies gik
en gade · gaden (the street) · gader (plural)

sentences.text: Hun havde ingen sko, og hendes fødder var meget kolde.
sentences.translation: She had no shoes, and her feet were very cold.

words.grammar: en fod · fødder (plural, irregular) · fødderne (the feet)
kold (common sg.) · koldt (neuter sg.) · kolde (pl./def.)

sentences.text: Pigen solgte svovlstikker, men ingen ville købe dem.
sentences.translation: The girl sold matches, but no one wanted to buy them.

words.grammar: en svovlstik · svovlstikker (plural) · old-fashioned word for matches
ville (modal: want to/would) · ville ikke / ingen ville = no one wanted to

sentences.text: Hun var bange for at gå hjem uden penge.
sentences.translation: She was afraid to go home without money.

words.grammar: være bange for + at-infinitive = to be afraid to (do something)
uden penge = without money · opposite of med (with)

sentences.text: Til sidst satte hun sig ned i et hjørne.
sentences.translation: Finally she sat herself down in a corner.

words.grammar: fixed adverbial phrase · til (to) + sidst (last)
et hjørne · hjørnet (the corner)

sentences.text: Hun tændte en svovlstik for at blive varm.
sentences.translation: She lit a match to get warm.

words.grammar: tænde (to light) · tændte (past) · har tændt (perfect) · weak verb
for at + infinitive = in order to · blive varm = to become warm (change of state)

sentences.text: I lyset så hun en varm kakkelovn.
sentences.translation: In the light she saw a warm stove.

words.grammar: en kakkelovn · a traditional Danish wood-burning stove
se (to see) · så (past) · har set (perfect) · strong verb

sentences.text: Hun tændte flere svovlstikker og så smukke billeder.
sentences.translation: She lit more matches and saw beautiful pictures.

words.grammar: flere = comparative of mange (many) · used for both common and neuter plural
et billede · billeder (plural)

sentences.text: I det sidste lys så hun sin bedstemor, som hun elskede meget.
sentences.translation: In the last light she saw her grandmother, whom she loved very much.

words.grammar: elske (to love) · elskede (past) · har elsket (perfect) · weak verb
en bedstemor · bedstemoren/bedstemoderen (the grandmother)

sentences.text: Bedstemoren tog hende blidt i hånden.
sentences.translation: Her grandmother gently took her by the hand.

words.grammar: blid (gentle, adj.) · blidt (adverb/neuter form)
en hånd · hånden (the hand) · i hånden = by the hand

sentences.text: Om morgenen fandt folk den lille pige med et smil på læberne.
sentences.translation: In the morning people found the little girl with a smile on her lips.

words.grammar: et smil · smilet (the smile) · på læberne = on her lips
en læbe · læber (plural) · læberne (the lips, def. pl.)

metadata.adaptedFrom: Adapted from H.C. Andersen, Den lille pige med svovlstikkerne (1845), simplified for A1 learners

grammarPoints.exampleSentence: Det var koldt, og sneen faldt over byen.
grammarPoints.explanation: Danish uses the dummy subject "det" for weather and general states, similar to English "it" in "it was cold". The adjective after være takes the neuter form (koldt), since det is grammatically neuter.

grammarPoints.exampleSentence: Hun tændte en svovlstik for at blive varm.
grammarPoints.explanation: "For at" introduces the purpose of an action, followed directly by an infinitive verb. It answers the question "why?": she lit the match — why? — for at blive varm (in order to get warm).

Ville is the past tense of vil (will/want to) and is used here to mean "wanted to". Combined with ingen (no one), "ingen ville" means "no one wanted to" — the modal is followed directly by an infinitive, with no "at".
